test_title: PYST 13: Selection Post (Higher Secondary Level) - English Language (Held On 24 Jul, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: english
question:
A sentence is provided in indirect speech. From the four given options, choose the one that most accurately conveys the sentence in its corresponding direct speech.

He said that he was feeling unwell.
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Direct Speech:** He said, "I am feeling unwell."
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **"was feeling" becomes "am feeling"**
 
 
• In the transition from indirect to direct speech, we reverse the "backshift." Since the indirect speech uses the **Past Continuous** ("was feeling"), the direct speech must use the **Present Continuous** ("am feeling").
 
 
 
• **Pronoun "he" becomes "I"**
 
 
• The pronoun **"he"** in the reported clause refers to the speaker, so it changes back to the first-person pronoun **"I"** in direct speech.
 
 
 
• **Punctuation:**
 
 
• Direct speech requires the use of a comma after the reporting verb and the placement of the spoken words within quotation marks, starting with a capital letter.
 
 
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"He said, “I am feeling unwell.”"*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2:** "He said, 'I will feel unwell.'" 

 
 
• **Error:** Uses the future tense, which would have been reported as "would be feeling" or "would feel."
 
 
 
• **Option 3:** "He said, 'I have felt unwell.'" 
 
 
• **Error:** Uses the Present Perfect tense, which would change to the Past Perfect ("had felt") in indirect speech.
 
 
 
• **Option 4:** "He said, 'I felt unwell.'" 
 
 
• **Error:** Uses the Past Simple tense. In indirect speech, this typically shifts to the Past Perfect ("had felt").
